.scratch/veridian/acceptance.yaml - the criterion read contains: 67/67, a literal that was true when it was written and is a second place the criterion count has to be edited
D:/all_projects/Veridian/core/validation/assertions.ts - matches is pattern.test(actual), so the count can be asserted as an invariant rather than as a literal
.scratch/veridian/state/runs/run-20260917-062028-eb3d8a/result.json - the earlier PASS 8/8, which is what ruled out a systematic failure of the two node criteria
scripts/traceability.js - the gate prints the number it declared and the number it cited, which is what makes the invariant expressible
evidence: $ node scripts/traceability.js -> criteria declared : 71 (docs/END-STATE.md); criteria cited : 71/71 by 59 requirement headings; OK - every criterion is cited and every cited test path exists; exit 0

$ node D:/all_projects/Veridian/cli/veridian.ts validate --no-memory --goal .scratch/veridian/goal.yaml --state-dir .scratch/veridian/state -> PASS (COMPLETED, 1 iteration(s)), 8/8 mandatory criteria passed, exit 0

The count in AC-007 was a snapshot of docs/END-STATE.md taken when it held 67 criteria; four more were added with the capture-on-by-default change set, so the criterion failed a tree that satisfies the requirement it checks. questions.doesNotEstablish: That Veridian ran any browser criterion: browser is disabled in environment.yaml and this run loaded no harness, so the two browser-manual gates remain out of band and quoted rather than executed. questions.question: docs/PROTOCOL.md section 3.2, docs/END-STATE.md open risk 6 and docs/RETENTION.md all describe the capture endpoint's refusal as a single PII precondition triggered by a phone number or an email address, yet a memory note was refused twice in a row while two of its neighbours stored. Is the documented trigger incomplete, and if so what is the actual rule?
artifactsTried: docs/PROTOCOL.md section 3.2 - its table names four patterns and its prose says a phone number or an email address, and its second consequence forbids the extension from pre-filtering, redacting or rewriting a capture to get past the precondition, so the finding had to be recorded without weakening that sentence
docs/END-STATE.md open risk 6 and docs/RETENTION.md - both describe the same single precondition in the same two terms, which is why the defect was in three documents rather than one
the MCP add tool - it reported a bare refusal with no body at all, which is what made a content refusal look like an authorization failure and is why the first two writes were misread
curl.exe issued against the same endpoint - it returns the refusal body, and the body names the pattern it matched, which is the one artifact that turned a behaviour table into a stated rule
a controlled minimal pair through the tool - the same sentence written twice with one token differing, one stored and one refused
twelve single-token probes through curl.exe, one variable per request, which pinned the contiguous digit threshold at exactly ten digits and showed the dashed form is not phone-shaped
a bisection of the refused note into halves and then quarters, which located the trigger in one token and cleared its length, its subject and its hex-shaped commit reference
docs/END-STATE.md - read to confirm that the refused token is one of its own section numbers, which is why an amendment that quotes it cannot be written down as a memory
evidence: $ curl.exe -s -X POST /memory/add with an upper-case letter and exactly two digits, delimited on both sides -> 403 {success:false,error:precondition blocked: PHI risk=0.85 patterns:[PHI:E13]}
$ the same request with that token carrying a decimal extension -> 403 patterns:[PHI:E13.9], reported whole

$ the same request with the letter lower-case, with one digit, with three digits, and with two letters then two digits -> 200 each, so the PHI match is case-sensitive and delimited rather than a prefix

$ the same request with a six-six dashed token -> 403 patterns:[PII:123456-1234]; with an eight-six token -> 403 patterns:[PII:345678-1234], so the reporter consumes ten digits including the separators and slides along a longer run to find them
$ the same request with one digit lower-case and a bare ten-digit run -> 403 patterns:[PII:1234567890], and with nine contiguous digits -> 200, so the contiguous threshold is exactly ten
$ a body of two thousand one hundred and sixty characters holding no matching token -> 200; the identical body with an eight-six token appended -> 403, which rules out length as the trigger
$ a successful write -> 200 carrying warning [{action:noted, id:..., overlap_ratio:66, target:...}], so a stored record can still carry a near-duplicate advisory without being rejected or merged
$ node scripts/traceability.js -> exit 0; $ node scripts/clarity.js -> exit 0
questions.resolution: The documented trigger was incomplete in three documents at once, and the correction is a second precondition rather than a wider first one. The refusal that started this was PHI, not PII: the runtime applies two preconditions, each names the pattern it matched, and PHI is keyed on a code shape rather than on numbers - an upper-case letter followed by exactly two digits, delimited, is refused, while the lower-case form, the one-digit form, the three-digit form and the two-letter form all store. The PII precondition the document already had is real and separate, at risk 0.90 against the PHI precondition's 0.85, and its published phone example is correct; what the document was missing is that its dashed form is not phone-shaped, since the runtime reports ten digits including the separators for a six-six token and slides to find a ten-digit window inside an eight-six one, while a date, a five-four pair and a nine-one pair are not matched at all. What made this critical rather than cosmetic is the collision: the repository's own end-state document numbers its host-registration section with a token of exactly the PHI shape, so a note quoting it cannot be stored as a memory, and the same class of token - a two-digit code or reference - is ordinary conversational text where a phone number is not. Three things were therefore changed and one was deliberately not. docs/PROTOCOL.md section 3.2 now records both preconditions, keeps the runtime's own printed pattern literals as the evidence rather than asserting a regular expression, and states that the refusal is not length-shaped and that a stored record may carry a near-duplicate warning. docs/END-STATE.md open risk 6 and its live-verification row now name both preconditions. The rule that the extension must never pre-filter, redact or rewrite a capture to get past either precondition is unchanged and unweakened, and no file under src/ was touched: the question was what the contract says, and the answer is more of it rather than different behaviour.
questions.doesNotEstablish: That these are the only preconditions. Two were observed and one of them was undocumented until this entry, so a third that no probe here reached may exist, and the reading is by construction limited to what was probed. The PHI rule is stated as the five payloads that were tested and not as an expression, and which fields are scanned was not established either - PII was previously verified against actor and target, and every PHI probe varied target alone, so a producer that puts the same token in an id or an action has not been measured. It does not establish the relative likelihood of either refusal on real captured text, only the shape of the token each one matches. And it does not begin to specify what the extension should do about a refusal: classification, counting apart from a transient failure and reporting the runtime's own error string verbatim remain cortexbridge-retention-boundary task 5.2's, and this change amended documentation only.

questions.question: The manual-add screen failed on a stub that answered curl, while an independent ADD_MEMORY sent from the same extension page was acknowledged. Is the popup's transport broken?
artifactsTried: scripts/browser-gate.mjs - the stub's own request log showed only OPTIONS /health and OPTIONS /memory/add and never a GET or a POST, so the fetch never completed
public/manifest.json - host_permissions is pinned to http://127.0.0.1:3030/*, so a stub on an ephemeral port is a different origin and the extension page must pass a preflight
docs/END-STATE.md G7 - a non-loopback host in host_permissions is a regression, so moving the stub onto 3030 or widening the manifest was not available
tests/helpers/http.ts - the unit harness stubs fetch outright, which is why the same code path is green in jsdom and could not have shown this
evidence: the stub before the fix -> seen = [OPTIONS /health 0B, OPTIONS /memory/add 0B], every fetch rejected as a failure to fetch, against a stub that was answering curl on the same port
the wire after the stub answered the preflight -> OPTIONS /health, GET /health, OPTIONS /memory/add, POST /memory/add 118B, then POST /memory/add 112B
$ npm run test:browser -> 37/37 checks passed, exit 0, with the click's POST matched by payload rather than by position in the log
questions.resolution: The transport was never broken; the harness was. A stub on an ephemeral port is cross-origin from an extension page because host_permissions is deliberately pinned to port 3030, so the browser sent a preflight the stub did not answer and every request died before reaching the product. The stub now answers OPTIONS with 204 plus the CORS headers and spreads the same headers into every reply. It is recorded because the failure mode is misleading in a specific way: a refused preflight surfaces as an unqualified fetch failure, which reads as a transport fault inside the extension and sends a reader to the wrong file.
questions.doesNotEstablish: That the extension works against a real core on a host the manifest does not cover. If anything it shows the opposite: host_permissions is loopback-only and pinned to one port, so a user who points the extension at another host relies on that host answering CORS, and no check in this repository covers that case.

questions.question: The popup's Add button was present, its click was raised, and an independent ADD_MEMORY from the same page was acknowledged - yet no POST /memory/add came from the click. Which layer dropped it?
artifactsTried: src/popup.ts - the DOMContentLoaded handler awaits refreshHealth, refreshEgressBanner, refreshCaptureStatus and refreshIndexStatus before it binds any control
public/popup.html - index-note is emitted empty and is filled by refreshIndexStatus, the last of those awaits, which makes it the only in-page signal that binding has happened

evidence: the run before the fix -> the independent probe reported acknowledged = true and the wire showed POST /memory/add 112B, while the click's own record was null, so the channel worked and the click had produced nothing

questions.doesNotEstablish: That no user can hit the same window. An extension page paints before its handlers bind, so a click landing inside those few milliseconds is lost; the window is two local message round trips, and no claim is made that a person can reach it, only that the harness used to sit inside it.

artifactsTried: openspec/changes/cortexbridge-perception-layer/tasks.md section 10.15 - it recorded the gate as not approached, and the obstacle it named was tooling: a browser that cannot host dist/ cannot observe a capture at all
tests/fixtures/<provider>/conversation.html - every fixture carries the same four turns in the same order under the same roles

questions.doesNotEstablish: That a live signed-in provider page behaves the same.
